sites.functional_impact_measured: Folding and trafficking: NOT PERTURBED — multiple studies explicitly state the tag 'neither affects the processing nor the trafficking of the protein' (PMC3563111) and 'has no effect on PMP22 trafficking or function' (PMC7322011). Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized immunofluorescence and flow cytometry with anti-myc antibody (PMC9860121). Complex glycosylation (Endo H resistance) confirmed for the tagged construct (PMC13382790 context). Function: NOT PERTURBED per PMC7322011 and PMC9860121.
sites.rationale: PMC13382790 explicitly names the junction as between residues 125 and 126 in ECL2. Python verification confirms: seq[124]='H' (His125) and seq[125]='L' (Leu126), matching the canonical sequence exactly. ECL2 spans residues 117–133 (authoritative topology); the insertion site is 9 residues from TM3 (ends at 116) and 9 residues from TM4 (starts at 134), both well above the >=3 residue minimum. The myc tag (10 aa) was tolerated; an ALFA tag with GS linkers (~15–23 aa) is of comparable or slightly larger size and is plausible given the demonstrated loop flexibility. The HA-tag ledger lines from PMC3563111 name only the loop (ECL2) without pinning a residue; they corroborate the loop's tolerance but do not constitute a separate junction. The C-terminal GFP (PMC11700639) and C-terminal ALFA (DOI:10.1101/2025.09.03.673966) tags were disqualified because the C-terminus (residues 157–160) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks. PMC13382790 reports a 10-residue myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop (ECL2) of human PMP22, synthesized as an intron-less ORF and subcloned into pCW57.1 for stable lentiviral expression. The same paper states this insertion was 'previously demonstrated to be non-perturbative of PMP22 folding and trafficking'. Multiple independent studies (PMC3563111, PMC7322011, PMC8191293, PMC3110552, PMC9860121, PMC13293285, PMC12881431) confirm that a myc or HA tag in ECL2 does not affect PMP22 processing, trafficking, or function, and that the tag is accessible to antibody labeling at the cell surface in non-permeabilized conditions (flow cytometry and immunofluorescence). The junction is 9 residues from TM3 end (residue 116) and 9 residues from TM4 start (residue 134), well within ECL2 (117–133). sources.claim: A DNA fragment encoding an intron-less human PMP22 ORF ( NM_153321 ) with an internal myc epitope tag (EQKLISEEDL) inserted between residues 125 and 126 was synthesized and subcloned into the pCW57.1 vector (Addgene, 41393) between NheI and AgeI restriction sites (Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT)).

literature_notes: Ledger lines considered and not proposed as separate sites: (1) PMC3563111 HA tag in ECL2 — names only the loop, not a residue; supports the same ECL2 region as the validated site but does not constitute a second pinned junction. (2) PMC7322011, PMC8191293, PMC3110552, PMC9860121, PMC13293285, PMC12881431 — all report myc tags in ECL2 without pinning a residue; they corroborate the validated site. (3) PMC11700639 C-terminal GFP — disqualified: the C-terminus (residues 157–160) is intracellular per authoritative topology; a tag there is not on the extracellular face. (4) DOI:10.1101/2025.09.03.673966 C-terminal ALFA tag — disqualified for the same reason; despite the non-permeabilized immunofluorescence showing PM localization of the protein, the ALFA tag itself is on the intracellular C-terminus and would not be accessible from the extracellular face. (5) PMC13293285 N41Q-myc and PMC12881431 N41Q-myc — the myc tag position is not stated in these quotes; N41Q refers to a glycosylation-deficient mutation in ECL1, not the tag location. No ECL1 insertion site can be pinned from these lines.
